input.question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?
input.ground_truth: It’s just tradition at this point. At one point in history encores were real but now every band just does it because it’s the thing every other band does. There are exceptions though, I’ve seen Bad Religion headline numerous times going through a 25-30 song set and just end it with no encore. The Supersuckers announce its time for “the fake encore” about 3 songs from the end...

Question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a game at school. You play your best songs, and everyone cheers and claps. But then, the bell rings and you have to stop. But your friends really, really want to hear one more song! So, you all come back out and play one more song just for them. That extra song at the end is called an "encore."

Now, when big music groups (called bands) play at concerts, they sometimes pretend like they're going to leave after their last song. But the crowd keeps cheering and cheering, so the band comes back out and plays a few more songs. Sometimes, the band plans this in advance—they know they're going to come back for a special extra song or two. This makes the crowd happy and gives everyone a fun surprise ending to the show!
